I am Zhang Guoqiang. I am 74 years old and I have farmed this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it before me. My sons went to the city twenty years ago. I am alone now, but I still work the 5 mu I have left — the rest I gave to my nephew to manage.

I know only one way to farm: wheat in winter, corn in summer. That is what this land does. That is what I do. Everyone in our village does the same. The soil here is flat and deep and it grows both well.

For wheat I already put the seeds in last October. Now it is spring and I must irrigate and put on the urea — I do this three times for wheat because water is what limits us here. The well pump is old but it still works. I buy diammonium phosphate at planting time and urea for top-dressing. I use about two bags of urea per mu — my neighbor uses the same and he has good harvests. I know the extension station people say use less nitrogen, but I am not going to risk my harvest on their advice. A bad year and I eat poorly.

For corn I wait until after I cut the wheat in June, then I plant right away. I buy the hybrid seeds from the village cooperative shop — the same kind I bought last year, Zhengdan 958, the shopkeeper says it is reliable. I rotate tilling with a small machine my nephew lets me borrow. I irrigate two or three times depending on the rain.

I cannot do no-tillage alone — I do not have the right machine — so I use rotary tillage. For pesticides I spray once or twice when I see aphids or rust on the wheat. On corn I spray for the armyworm if it appears.

I do not expect a great harvest. At my age I am satisfied with enough.
